sections.html: Origin: Indonesia (Sulawesi). Females reach a maximum length of around 6 cm; males always stay smaller. Water temperature 24–28°C, pH 7–8.5.
This species of halfbeak comes from Sulawesi (formerly Celebes), Indonesia. It was described scientifically only in 2012.
Water temperature should be between 24 and 28°C. Neutral or slightly alkaline water (pH between 7 and 8.5) is the best choice.

Feeding is easy, as the fish readily take flakes from the water surface. Additionally, freeze-dried food items should be fed. The fish usually feed on sinking food only when they feel absolutely safe.
The livebearing halfbeaks are best kept in larger groups (10 specimens or more); they are then comparatively peaceful towards each other.

Males stay smaller than females. The anal fin of males is modified into an andropodium, which serves for internal fertilization of the females. It has a species-specific structure which usually also prevents hybrids from occurring.

N. rex is most easily distinguished by coloration from the quite similar N. ebrardtii: N. rex has yellow ventral fins (reddish-orange in N. ebrardtii), a red lower beak (in N. ebrardtii the lower beak is the same colour as the body), and black-bordered fins, which N. ebrardtii lacks. Other differences exist but are not visible in live animals.

Etymology: Nomorhamphus means "with about equal beaks"; ebrardtii is a dedication to "Geheimrat" (privy councillor) Ebrardt; rex means "king", chosen because the fish's teeth recall those of the dinosaur Tyrannosaurus rex.

Suggested common name: Red-black halfbeak.
